questions.question: 'Neo-Malthusian Theory' is associated with which of the following?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Neo-Malthusianism is the advocacy of population control programs, to ensure resources for current and future populations.
 
• This theory believes earth's resources can only support a finite population and that limited resources keep the population in check and reduce economic growth, therefore, growth should be controlled.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Definition of Inflation: 

Inflation refers to the general rise in the price level in an economy.

 
• An increase in inflation leads to a fall in the purchasing power of a currency as the commodities and prices get higher.
 
• In simple words, we would be able to purchase only fewer items for the same amount of money.

questions.question: How many Fundamental Duties are mentioned in Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
Option **4** is correct, i.e. __**Eleven**__.

There are 11 fundamental duties, they are:

__
 
• Abide by the Constitution and respect national flag & National Anthem.
 
• Follow ideals of the freedom struggle.
 
• Protect sovereignty & integrity of India.
 
• Defend the country and render national services when called upon.
 
• Sprit of a common brotherhood.
 
• Preserve composite culture.
 
• Preserve the natural environment.
 
• Develop a scientific temper.
 
• Safeguard public property.
 
• Strive for excellence.
 
• Duty fo all parents/guardians to send their children in the age group of 6-14 years to school.

Extra facts:

 
• The Swaran Singh Committee is related to the Fundamental Duties in India.
 
• On the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, 11 Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 51A deals with the Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1976.
 
• The concept of fundamental duties of the Indian constitution was borrowed from the USSR(__Union of Soviet Socialist Republics__).__

questions.question: Part IV of constitution of India deals with which of the following?
questions.solution:

questions.question: Todar mal was the finance minister of which Mughal ruler?
questions.solution:
Raja Todar Mal was the __Finance Minister__ of the Mughal empire during **Akbar's reign.**

Raja Todar Mal:-

 
• He was one of the Navaratna's in Akbar's 'darbar'
 
• Raja Todar Mal introduced standard weights and measures, a land survey and settlement system, revenue districts and officers.
 
• He introduced a new system of revenue known as zabt and a system of taxation called dahshala.
 
• The Kashi Vishwanath Temple was rebuilt in 1585 by Todar Mal.
 
• The navratnas of Akbar were as follows: Raja Birbal, Tansen, Abul Fazal, Faizi, Raja Man Singh, Raja Todar Mal, Mullah Do Piaza, Fakir Aziao-Din, Abdul Rahim Khan-I-Khana.

questions.question: Gravitational force is maximum at which of the following place?
questions.solution:
• The gravitational force is highest at the two poles of the earth i.e. the North Pole and the South Pole.
 
• This is because centrifugal forces are absent at poles and are maximum at equator and they act against gravitation, also the Earth is not a perfect sphere and the distance to Earth is shorter at poles.

questions.question: Which of the following disease is caused by female Anopheles mosquito?
questions.solution: Malaria is an infectious disease caused by parasitic protozoans and is spread by vectors such as the female Anopheles mosquito. Malaria causes symptoms that typically include fever, tiredness, vomiting, and headaches.

questions.question: Which part of the plant gives us saffron?
questions.solution: Saffron is extracted from the stigma and styles of the plant, it is a spice that is used in Indian delicacies and is considered as one of the costliest spice in the world. It is widely found in Jammu and Kashmir in India.

questions.question: Which of the following transports water from the roots of the plant to its leaves?
questions.solution: Xylem is a transport tissue in vascular plants. Its basic function is to transport water from roots to shoots and leaves. It sometimes also helps in transporting certain minerals to various parts of the plant.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a vector quantity?
questions.solution: Speed is not a vector quantity because speed is the distance travelled in a unit time and a vector has to have magnitude as well as direction.

questions.question: At what temperature (in Fahrenheit) pure water freezes?
questions.solution: Pure water freezes at 32o Fahrenheit and 0o Celsius and 273.15 Kelvin. The boiling point of the pure water is 212o Fahrenheit.

questions.question: In which graphics, digital photos and scanned images are typically stored with extensions such as .bmp, .png, .jpg, .tif or.gif?
questions.solution: Bitmap is the format in which an image is shown and stored digitally. It comprises of various dots which together form the image. Such dots are called pixels, therefore, as the number of dots in an image increases the clarity of the image increases.

questions.question: Process of gaining electrons is known as _______.
questions.solution: Reduction is the chemical process of gaining electrons from other elements.

questions.question: Which of the following metal (shown by its symbol) is generally used for making filaments of bulb?
questions.solution: Tungsten is the element from which filaments of the light bulbs are made; this is because of their hardness and high density. Its symbol is ‘W’ because of its scientific name ‘Wolfram’.

questions.question: Which of the following trees shed their leaves once in a year?
questions.solution: Deciduous trees shed their leaves once in a year in winters to save water and to survive harsh weather. The trees that never shed leaves are called the Evergreen trees.

questions.question: The Entrepreneurship Development Scheme (EDS) has been launched under New Economy Development Policy (NEDP) on January 19, 2017 at ________.
questions.solution: NEDP is the economic policy rolled out by the Mizoram state government in 2016 to boost the agriculture in the state. Under this scheme EDS was launched in 2017 on January 19 in Aizawl.

questions.concept: Science Technology and Inventions, Famous People
questions.question: Who invented Dynamite?
questions.solution:
• Alfred Nobel was a Swedish inventor and businessman who invented dynamite that is used for explosions.
 
• He also established five Nobel Prizes in the field of peace, literature, physics, chemistry, and medicine to mark the contribution to mankind by people.

questions.question: 'Rovers cup' is associated with which of the following sport?
questions.solution: Rovers Cup was the annual football tournament held in India till 2001 after which it was discontinued. The last football club to win that tournament was Mohun Bagan AC.

questions.question: Dandia is a form of dance associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution: Dandiya or Dandiya Raas is the traditional folk dance of Gujarat which is performed with two sticks in the hands of two people. It is generally performed on the evenings of Navratri.

questions.concept: Art and Culture, Awards and Honours
questions.question: Who among the following was awarded with Dhronacharya Award 2016 in the field of 'Swimming (Lifetime)'?
questions.solution: Shri S. Pradeep Kumar is the head coach of India’s best swimming school in Bangalore and had produced more than 8000 swimmers out of which 4000 have won medals in national and international arena. He was awarded the Dronacharya Award (awarded to coaches of various sports in India) in 2016.

questions.question: 'Ace against Odds' is an autobiography of which sports person?
questions.solution: ‘Ace against odds’ is the autobiography of the Sania Mirza who is considered as the best female tennis player of India. Her autobiography was published in 2016. She was also ranked number 1 in doubles by WTA in 2015 for some time.

questions.question: Under the framework of the new partnership with which country, Victoria University will help India to Establish a National Sports University?
questions.solution: Victoria University of Australia will help India establish a National Sports University in Manipur. National Sports University Bill, 2017 has been proposed for this purpose.

questions.question: With which country India exchanged its border enclaves?
questions.solution: India and Bangladesh exchanged border enclaves that were disputed in 2015 by passing Land Boundary Agreement in May 2015. A total number of 111 enclaves were exchanged.
